Department Recommendation:  Authorize a sole source purchase to replace four (4) police services canines from Gold Coast K9 services in Ventura, CA, and the required supplies and training for a total project cost of $87,400. Appropriate an additional $10,300 in Asset Forfeiture Funds (621) and transfer funds from CIP CP0611 to CIP CP0747 so that all available funds are in a single account.

Summary: 
The Visalia Police Department has utilized the services of police service canines for more than 40 years. Police service canines have proven to be a valuable tool in enhancing officer and public safety through a variety of service applications such as their ability to search, track, assist in apprehensions of suspects, locate evidence, and as valuable community outreach assets.  Police service canines can be utilized to assist in searching, tracking, and locating persons or evidence beyond the abilities of their human partners and can also be deployed in situations to minimize risk to police officers, enhancing both officer and community safety.

Beyond this service, the Visalia Police Department has historically involved its police service canines in a variety of community outreach events and public engagements including, but not limited to: Coffee with a Cop, Hometown Heroes, and service club and school presentations. Police service canines have proven to be a great tool for making positive connections with the community and interactions with officers.

Currently the department has one police service canine assigned to the Patrol Division and it is nearing the end of its service career. These requested canines will be utilized in the Patrol Division to assist in searching for and locating individuals who are attempting to evade arrest and pose a risk to public safety. Additionally, the four police service canines will be cross-trained in scent detection; three in narcotics scent detection, and one in explosive scent detection.. 

The Visalia Police Department has been waiting for the new California POST guidelines regarding guidelines for Police K-9 units. These guidelines recommend minimum training and evaluation benchmarks for K-9 Patrol and Detection functions. The standards that were established by California POST were minimum standards for basic canine handler/team training, the deployment of canines during patrol operations, performance standards for Police Canines, and scent detection standards. The Visalia Police Department K9 Unit will meet or exceed all standards outlined in California POST K-9 Guidelines.

Background Discussion: 
The Visalia Police K9 Unit currently consists of two (2) police service canines and their officer handlers, a patrol canine and narcotics detection canine. The K9 Unit staffing levels historically consisted of six (6) patrol service canines and one (1) narcotics detection canine but five (5) of these police service canines have been retired over the last few years. This proposal seeks to replace four (4) of those previously retired of police service canines.

Gold Coast K-9 Services is the sole provider of monthly maintenance training to the Visalia Police Department K9 Unit (Gold Coast also provides training services to various other agencies in the Tulare/Kings Counties area). Additionally, Gold Coast K-9 Services sell an almost fully trained canine when it is assigned to the handler compared to the other California vendors that sell "green" dogs, meaning they have a very basic level of training. Gold Coast canines are trained to meet the requirements outlined by POST and will be ready to start training with the officer upon delivery. 

In addition, Gold Coast also deals in smaller numbers which means they can focus on quality and not quantity. The other vendors are importing larger number of canines for their accounts, which means the quality of canine can diminish. Gold Coast K-9 Services has provided maintenance training and Police Service Canine to the City of Visalia for several years. They are known for their professional services and commitment to providing the best canines for California Law Enforcement needs.

Fiscal Impact including annual maintenance and operating costs: 
There is a total budget of $77,146 to make this purchase, which is currently budgeted into two separate Asset Forfeiture accounts. CIP 6210/CP0747 has a budget of $61,000 and 6210/CP0611 has a remainder budget of $16,146 to replace canines from a previous budget year. Staff is requesting to transfer the funds from 6210/CP0611 to 6210/CP0747 and appropriate an additional $10,300 from the Asset Forfeiture Fund. 

The cost of the dogs will be offset by a donation of $27,341 which was received March 4, 2025, from the Friends of Police K-9 and community members, and a previous credit from Gold Coast. There is a total of 6 operable patrol vehicles dedicated to the K-9 unit, therefore, there is no need to purchase any vehicles. These specialized units are on a regular replacement schedule of 7 years, and 75,000 miles. The police canine vehicles are ready for use.

Summary: 
Staff requested Darden Architects to provide a design fee proposal and construction cost estimate for phase 3 of the Visalia civic center project. Staff is recommending that Council award a sole source design contract to Darden as the architectural and engineering consultant (A/E) for phase 3 based on their previous experience designing phases 1 & 2. The estimate included the base cost for an approximately 54,000 SF, 3-story office building, and optional costs for amenities including a police department (PD) training facility, caf� & patio space, health clinic, and the addition of a fourth floor for future growth space. These options were discussed and recommended for consideration by the staff involved in the civic center planning committee. It is anticipated that the plans, specifications and estimates (PS&E) phase of the project will last approximately 14 months from the time an agreement can be executed with the design consultant. 
 

Background Discussion: 
The Visalia civic center project was planned to be implemented and constructed in phases. Phase 1 consisted of constructing the Visalia emergency communications center (VECC), which was completed in 2018. Phase 2 is currently under construction and includes three buildings, the evidence storage and crime lab, public safety administration building and city council chambers, and is scheduled to be completed in July of 2027. The third and final phase of the civic center would consist of a new city hall building which may include amenities such as an on-site caf� and health clinic, and an optional police department training facility. The location of the proposed city hall building and PD training facility are shown on the civic center site plan (attached)

Darden led the A/E team for the initial civic center site planning and design, design of the VECC, and design of the public safety administration building, evidence building, and council chambers. Darden has already laid out the future building pad location for the city hall building and prepared the architectural details and features for all the civic center buildings. It is staff's recommendation to use Darden for phase 3 based on the extensive amount of work they have already completed on the civic center project. Darden's extensive experience with previous phases of the civic center will make design of phase 3 much more efficient. This is expected to result in significant savings in staff time during the course of design and it is also expected to expedite the design timeline for phase 3.   

Staff met with the civic center committee to discuss possible options to be included in phase 3. The following are some of the reasons why the committee is recommending the following options:

1. Fourth floor addition - Visalia is a strong and growing community and staff expects this to continue for many years. The committee feels as though it would be wise to allow for additional staff growth and/or opportunities for partnering with other businesses in the future. 
2. PD training facility/range - The police department this is a facility that is needed for development of police department staff. If this facility is designed now there may be possible grant opportunities in the future for a shovel ready project.
3. Caf�/patio - The committee believes that this is a good option to provide employees with needed amenities, a space for staff to enjoy a break and increase mental health wellness, and will aid in employee satisfaction resulting in a more efficient workforce. 
4. Health clinic - The committee believes this makes financial sense and that it would be well received by staff and their families. With an increasing number of staff members, it is anticipated that a larger space will be needed than what the city currently has available. 
     
Based on those discussions, it is recommended to design Phase 3 with the above mentioned options. It is more efficient to design the optional features now than to add them to the design documents later. The various optional features can be included in the final bid documents as alternate items if desired so the city can receive bids and make final decisions on the options based on the overall project cost.

Department Recommendation:  Staff recommends that City Council authorize the City Manager to award a 5-year sole source contract with Landia, Inc. to provide services to repair and, when necessary, replace submersible recycle pumps and mixers at the Visalia Water Reclamation Facility in an amount not to exceed $134,000 per year and $670,000 over the life of the contract.

Summary: 
The Visalia Water Reclamation Facility uses submersible recycle pumps and mixers in the aeration basins to support biological nutrient removal and reduce nitrogen in the wastewater. The aeration basins contain 4 recycle pumps and 12 mixers, and staff typically maintains 2 spare recycle pumps and 4 spare mixers to minimize downtime when equipment requires repair. Landia, Inc. is the sole provider of parts and repair services for this equipment. Approval of the proposed 5-year sole source contract will allow staff to obtain timely repairs and replacements, as needed, while maintaining critical process reliability.

Background Discussion: 
The Visalia Water Reclamation Facility relies on the aeration basin process to treat wastewater and meet regulatory requirements. The recycle pumps and mixers are critical components in this process because they help move and mix wastewater and mixed liquor within the aeration basins, supporting the biological conditions needed to reduce nitrogen before final treatment and discharge.

The facility currently has 4 Landia recycle pumps and 12 Landia mixers installed in the aeration basins. Due to the corrosive and demanding wastewater environment, the pumps and mixers periodically require maintenance, repair, or replacement. To reduce the risk of extended process downtime, staff typically keeps 2 spare recycle pumps and 4 spare mixers available so failed equipment can be removed from service and replaced while repairs are completed.

Landia, Inc. is the sole provider of parts and service for the Landia recycle pumps and mixers used at the WRF. Because the equipment is proprietary and must be repaired with the correct parts and technical expertise, a sole source contract is necessary to ensure repairs are performed properly and the equipment remains compatible with the existing aeration basin systems.

Under the proposed contract, Landia, Inc. will perform repairs on an as-needed basis. If a mixer or pump is inspected and determined to be beyond economical repair, Landia will provide a replacement unit. Establishing a 5-year contract will streamline procurement, reduce delays in obtaining parts and repair services, and support continued reliability of the WRF nitrogen removal process.

Annual spending with Landia over the past three fiscal years has averaged around $85,000. Staff estimates that an annual NTE of $134,000 should be enough to cover the worst-case scenario of needing several extensive repairs on each shelf-spare in a single year.


Fiscal Impact including annual maintenance and operating costs: The proposed 5-year sole source contract will have an annual not-to-exceed amount of $134,000 and a total not-to-exceed amount of $670,000 over the life of the contract.The total contract amount includes capacity for as-needed repairs and potential replacement of pumps or mixers that cannot be repaired during the contract term. Funds are budgeted annually in the Wastewater Fund (431) Capital Budget under CP0439. Costs will only be incurred as services, parts, or replacement units are needed.

Department Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council authorize the City Manager to issue a sole source purchase order to Cummins, Inc., for the commissioning and startup of the renewable power generation system (RPGS) at the Visalia Water Reclamation Facility, in the amount of $251,757, and the appropriation of $260,000 from Wastewater Fund 431 into CIP CP0323 to fund the commissioning scope.

Summary: 
The City of Visalia Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) requires final commissioning and startup of the renewable power generation system (RPGS), which has remained uncommissioned since installation due to SCR retrofit requirements and subsequent vendor scheduling limitations. Because the prior purchase order (P03454) and associated contract (C15051) are closed and cannot be amended, a new sole-source purchase order is required to authorize the Cummins final RPGS commissioning proposal. The original RPGS procurement and installation contract from 2018-2019 included only limited OEM start-up tasks and did not include full commissioning, emissions activation, or the multi-vendor integration now required to bring the system online. No remaining scope or budget exists under any earlier authorization.

This commissioning work must be procured as sole source because Cummins is the only vendor authorized and technically able to perform the integrated OEM commissioning sequence. "Technically able" means Cummins is the OEM responsible for all proprietary controls, emissions-control logic, SCR ammonia-dosing algorithms, blending-skid integration, protective relay coordination, and utility-compliance startup procedures, none of which can be accessed or configured by third-party vendors.

To complete the commissioning scope, the City will need to appropriate $260,000 from Wastewater Fund 431 into CIP CP0323, which will fund the purchase order amount and associated commissioning-related expenses.

Background Discussion: 
RPGS System Overview & Project History
The City of Visalia Water Reclamation Facility possesses a 1-megawatt renewable power generation system (RPGS) fueled by internally produced digester gas. Mechanical installation was completed in 2018; however, delays related to the Southern California Edison interconnect, along with updated regional air regulations from the Air Board required the installation of a selective catalytic reduction (SCR) emissions-control system, delaying startup. The RPGS represents a $4.01 million capital investment intended to offset electrical demand, reduce flaring, and improve environmental compliance.

Commissioning Delays & Readiness Timeline
Although the SCR system was installed in 2021, commissioning could not proceed due to digester-gas quality deficiencies and prerequisite system issues, which the City resolved between 2023 and 2026. Cummins verified the system as fully commissioned-ready on March 18, 2026. During this period, all prior commissioning attempts were suspended, and no remaining scope or budget existed under earlier authorizations.

Need for a New Sole-Source Purchase Order
The original 2018-19 procurement and installation contract included only limited OEM start-up tasks such as initial engine start procedures, basic loading tests, preliminary emissions checks, and operator training. These activities did not constitute full system commissioning and excluded SCR activation, blending-skid commissioning, switchgear protection tuning, emissions-compliance testing, and multi-vendor integration. Because these elements were never part of the original scope, no commissioning authority or funding exists within prior authorizations.

Because the generator, controls, SCR system, blending skid, and switchgear must all be commissioned together under Cummins' OEM procedures, the remaining work cannot be performed by third-party contractors. "Technically able" means Cummins is the OEM responsible for the generator engine, electronic controls, emissions-control logic, SCR ammonia-dosing algorithms, blending-skid integration requirements, protective-relay coordination, and utility-compliance startup procedures. No third party has access to Cummins' proprietary control software, parameter maps, emissions-tuning logic, load-management sequences, or generator-protection configurations needed to commission the RPGS safely and in compliance with Air District and utility requirements.

For these reasons, the commissioning effort requires a new sole-source purchase order with Cummins to complete the integrated OEM startup, tuning, emissions activation, and compliance testing needed to bring the system online.

The commissioning timeline and final pricing from Cummins were not available until after the FY 2026-27 capital budgets were submitted, so no funding was budgeted for commissioning in that fiscal cycle. An appropriation of $260,000 from Wastewater Fund 431 into CP0323 is now required to fund the commissioning scope.

Commissioning Scope & Vendor Activities
For clarity, adder04 (formerly referenced as adder04 Rev5) is now titled "Cummins final RPGS commissioning proposal" and represents the complete, modernized commissioning scope. This proposal defines all 2026 labor, travel, testing, tuning, and multi-vendor integration tasks required to bring the RPGS into compliance with current regulatory and utility requirements.

The proposal mobilizes four specialty vendors under Cummins, ACS/Preferred, PEECO, Miratech, and Cummins OEM commissioning staff, to complete First Fire, load tuning, blending-skid commissioning, SCR setup and activation, emissions tuning, utility witness testing, and final compliance documentation.

The City conducted technical and financial reconciliation of all prior commission-related purchase orders, including correcting historical pricing discrepancies, confirming 2026-only costs, and validating vendor availability. This work produced the fully reconciled, final not-to-exceed total of $251,757.00.

Catalyst Work & October 2026 Commissioning Schedule
Miratech will load the catalyst blocks, replace dosing-system components, and complete SCR pre-commissioning during the week of October 5, 2026, ensuring readiness for SCR activation.

Commissioning remains scheduled for October 5-23, 2026, and includes:
� First fire
� Load tuning
� Blending-skid commissioning
� Catalyst loading
� SCR activation
� Emissions tuning
� Utility witness testing
� Final documentation and demobilization

Approval of the new purchase order secures the vendor schedule and allows the RPGS to be commissioned and brought online.

Fiscal Impact: 
The amount for the Cummins final RPGS commissioning proposal is $251,757 and will be issued as a sole-source purchase order. Cummins is the only vendor authorized and technically able to perform the integrated OEM commissioning, controls configuration, emissions-tuning, and SCR activation work required to place the RPGS into compliant operation. "Technically able" means that Cummins alone controls the proprietary engine ECU software, generator parameter maps, emissions-control logic, SCR dosing algorithms, blending-skid integration protocols, and utility-protection settings needed to commission the system. To fund the commissioning scope, the City will appropriate $260,000 from Wastewater Fund 431 into CP0323. This appropriation will fund the purchase order and all associated commissioning-related expenses; catalyst block loading and SCR pre-commissioning are included within the existing Miratech cost. All prior RPGS-related expenditures have been reconciled, and no duplicative costs are included.

Prior Council Action:                                                                                                        
July 2015, the City Council authorized the award of a contract for the procurement of the Renewable Power Generation System (RPGS) for the Water Reclamation Facility. The action approved the purchase and delivery of the 1-megawatt digester-gas-fueled generator set, controls, and associated system components at a cost of approximately $5.8 million. This authorization represents the City's initial capital investment in the RPGS and is reflected in the project cost ledger under the 2015 equipment purchase.  

August 2016, the City Council approved amendments to the construction and engineering contracts supporting the installation of the Renewable Power Generation System as part of the Water Conservation Plant Upgrade program. These amendments authorized additional construction services, integration work, and engineering support related to the RPGS facilities and equipment. These costs are included within the historic capital expenditures and are reconciled in the project ledger.                                            

May 20, 2019, the City Council authorized the design, engineering, and procurement activities necessary to install a Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) emissions control system on the RPGS generator. The authorization included engineering services for SCR design and construction support, as well as the purchase of the SCR equipment itself. The action also approved the transfer of approximately $1 million to establish a dedicated capital project for SCR implementation. These costs are fully reflected in the ledger under the 2019 SCR procurement.                                                                                               

May 3, 2021, the City Council approved the sole-source installation of a new SCR system on the 1-megawatt generator at a cost of approximately $1.15 million, and appropriated an additional $670,000 from the Wastewater Treatment Plant Fund. This action initiated the SCR installation work that remains part of the current commissioning scope. All expenditures associated with this authorization are already captured in the project ledger under the SCR procurement and construction history.                                

May 6, 2024, the City Council approved a change order in the amount of $196,619 for generator repairs and maintenance performed by Cummins Pacific, and appropriated $200,000 from the Wastewater Treatment Plant Fund. These repairs-implemented as part of the Adder02 scope-were required to restore the RPGS generator to commissioning-ready condition. These expenditures are already reconciled in the project ledger and are not duplicated in the Adder04 cost.
  
Alternatives: 
1. Do Not Approve the Cummins Final RPGS Commissioning Proposal - Not recommended. This would delay startup, prolong flare use, and increase regulatory exposure.  

2. Postpone Startup to a Later Year - Not recommended. This risks equipment degradation, vendor scheduling conflicts, and higher future costs.  

Rebid Not Included: A rebid is not feasible. No third-party vendor is authorized or qualified to perform the required OEM commissioning sequence, and both the prior contract and purchase order are closed. Only Cummins can provide the integrated commissioning, controls, emissions, and tuning work required for regulatory compliance.

Department Recommendation:  Staff recommends that Council approve a purchase order to APGN Inc. dba APG-Neuros in the amount of $285,843.25, including estimated sales tax, for the purchase of one high-speed turbo blower for the Visalia Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) and appropriate $500,000 from the Wastewater Fund.

Summary: 
Staff is requesting approval to purchase one APG-Neuros high-speed turbo blower and to complete the related installation work as the first unit in a planned multi-year replacement of the WRF's existing Aerzen aeration blowers. The Aerzen units have experienced recurring reliability problems and have required significant maintenance, replacement parts, and temporary rental equipment to maintain adequate aeration capacity. The WRF currently operates APG-Neuros blowers for membrane bioreactor (MBR) air scour service, and those units have performed reliably with relatively few issues.

The proposed purchase will begin standardizing the WRF's aeration blower equipment around a manufacturer with which staff already has successful operating experience. APG-Neuros has proposed one NX450-C090A high-speed turbo blower, related accessories, louver inlet, discharge check valve, manual discharge butterfly valve with chainwheel operator, EPDM discharge duct expansion joint, blow-off silencer, internal harmonic filter, start-up, and training services for a subtotal of $263,450 before sales tax. With estimated sales tax of $22,393.25, the total APG-Neuros purchase order amount is $285,843.25. Staff estimates that the installation will cost approximately $180,000. Staff is requesting a total appropriation of $500,000 to cover the blower purchase, installation, and a $34,156.75 contingency for unanticipated change orders.

Background Discussion: 
The WRF relies on turbo blowers to supply air to the biological treatment process. Adequate aeration is necessary to maintain treatment performance and meet the facility's nitrogen and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) discharge requirements. Loss of sufficient blower capacity can create an immediate operational and regulatory risk.

The WRF currently has five Aerzen turbo blowers that were originally manufactured by KTurbo. Over the past several years, these units have experienced repeated failures and have required substantial maintenance and replacement parts. Most recently, multiple blower variable frequency drives (VFDs), or inverters, failed, reducing available permanent aeration capacity and requiring the City to rent a temporary Aerzen blower. A repaired inverter installed on one of the permanent units failed again only five days after installation, further demonstrating the reliability concerns associated with the existing equipment.

Because of these recurring issues, staff has evaluated a long-term transition away from the Aerzen units. Staff intends to replace the existing Aerzen aeration blowers with APG-Neuros units over the next several years as funding becomes available and as existing units reach the point where continued repair is no longer cost-effective.

The WRF already uses APG-Neuros blowers to provide air scour for the MBR process. Those units have performed well and have had relatively few reliability issues. Standardizing future aeration blower replacements with APG-Neuros equipment will allow operations and maintenance staff to build on their existing familiarity with the manufacturer's controls, operating characteristics, maintenance requirements, and technical support. It will also reduce the long-term complexity associated with maintaining multiple blower manufacturers and equipment platforms.

The proposed NX450-C090A blower is a 450-horsepower high-speed turbo blower sized for the WRF's aeration system. At the City's design condition, the proposed unit is rated to deliver approximately 7,769 standard cubic feet per minute at 11.4 pounds per square inch gauge. The blower package includes a permanent magnet synchronous motor, air bearings, variable speed drive, Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC-based controls, remote monitoring capability, instrumentation, filtration, and a sound enclosure. The purchase also includes related accessories, an internal harmonic filter, start-up, and training services.

The NX450-C090A blower is similar in design and operating concept to the blowers currently used by the WRF for membrane bioreactor (MBR) air scour service. Although the proposed aeration blower is larger and sized for a different process duty, it uses the same general high-speed turbo blower platform. The unit includes a permanent magnet synchronous motor, air bearing, forged impeller, high-performance variable speed drive/inverter, local control panel, remote-control capability, onboard pressure and temperature instrumentation, built-in flow calculation, filtration, vibration isolation, surge protection, and sound enclosure. These are the same general types of components and operating features that make APG-Neuros units distinct from conventional positive displacement or older turbo blower systems.

Because both applications use APG-Neuros high-speed turbo blower technology, staff expects meaningful overlap in operator familiarity, maintenance approach, controls philosophy, troubleshooting practices, and manufacturer support. The aeration basin blower will serve a different process function than the MBR air scour blowers—supplying biological process air to the aeration basins rather than scour air to the membranes—but the core equipment design is similar enough that standardizing on APG-Neuros reduces the number of blower platforms WRF staff must support. This allows operations and maintenance staff to build on their successful experience with the existing MBR air scour blowers while beginning the phased replacement of the less reliable Aerzen aeration blower units.

Staff is requesting a sole source purchase because the City has selected APG-Neuros as the equipment platform for the phased replacement of the existing Aerzen blowers. The requested equipment is proprietary APG-Neuros equipment supplied by the manufacturer. Purchasing a different manufacturer's blower through a competitive process would not accomplish the City's goal of standardizing future blower replacements around the APG-Neuros platform and would introduce another equipment type into the WRF. The City's existing successful experience with APG-Neuros equipment, combined with the operational and maintenance benefits of standardization, supports the sole source request.

The manufacturer anticipates providing submittals within two to four weeks after receipt of the purchase order and shipping the blower approximately 16 to 20 weeks after approval of the submittals. The new blower will require installation before it can be placed into service. The unit will be installed in the space currently occupied by Blower No. 3, which is out of commission. In order to install the new unit, a contractor will be procured to remove the existing blower and associated piping/silencer connections, receive and set the City-furnished APG-Neuros blower, demolish and replace the equipment housekeeping pad, fabricate and install new 16-inch and 6-inch carbon steel piping, perform pressure testing, insulate and coat new piping, complete required electrical modifications, coordinate programming and start-up support, and coordinate commissioning with the equipment manufacturer. Staff estimates that this scope of work will cost $180,000.

Fiscal Impact including annual maintenance and operating costs: The total project cost, before contingency, is $465,843.25. This consists of the APG-Neuros blower purchase in the amount of $285,843.25, including $263,450 for the blower equipment and related manufacturer services plus estimated sales tax of $22,393.25, and the installation estimate of $180,000. Staff is requesting an appropriation of $500,000 from the Wastewater Fund (431) to cover the total project cost and an additional contingency of $34,156.75 to account for any unanticipated change orders during installation. The blower will replace existing aeration equipment, and there are no additional staffing costs associated with this action. Routine maintenance and electrical costs will be paid from existing WRF operating accounts.

Prior Council Action: N/A
  
Alternatives: Council may direct staff to continue repairing the existing Aerzen blowers or direct staff to pursue a different procurement approach. These alternatives are not recommended because of the recurring reliability issues with the existing equipment and the operational benefits of standardizing future replacements with APG-Neuros units.

Recommended Motion (and Alternative Motions if expected):
..recommendation
I move to approve a purchase order to APGN Inc. dba APG-Neuros in the amount of $285,843.25 for the purchase of one high-speed turbo blower for the Visalia Water Reclamation Facility and appropriate $500,000 from the Wastewater Fund.
